args.title: payments-api v5.1.0 elevated error rate (18%) — rolled back to v5.0.0
args.summary: Since the morning deploy of v5.1.0 to production (us-east, us-west, eu-west), payments-api has been throwing errors at an 18% error rate with all three regions reporting unhealthy. v5.1.0 was recorded as "degraded" in the release history. Service was rolled back to v5.0.0, the most recent release healthy in production; post-rollback status is healthy with error rate down to 0.2%. Incident opened to track customer impact during the ~error window this morning, confirm full recovery across regions, and gate re-deployment of v5.1.0 pending root-cause analysis.

trace.final:
Done. Summary:

**Service identified:** The name `payments` doesn't exist in the runbook — the actual service is **`payments-api`**. That was unhealthy (`healthy: false`, **18% error rate**) on **v5.1.0** in all three production regions (us-east, us-west, eu-west).

**Release history:**
| Version | Status | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| v5.0.0 | healthy | most recent healthy production release |
| v5.1.0 | degraded | this morning's deploy |

**Rollback:** Rolled `payments-api` back to **v5.0.0** across all production regions. Verified post-rollback: `healthy: true`, error rate **0.2%** (down from 18%).

**Incident:** Opened **INC-0001**, SEV2, on-call paged — covering the customer-impact window this morning and gating any re-deploy of v5.1.0 pending root-cause analysis.

Two things worth flagging for follow-up:
- v5.1.0 has now been rolled back once due to production degradation; re-deploying it would need change-manager approval as a version that has never been healthy in production.
- The original request named a service that doesn't exist, so I inferred `payments-api`. If you actually meant a different payments-adjacent service, let me know and I'll check it — no changes were made to anything else.
